Ang growth hormone gikan sa pituitary motabang sa pagtaas ug pagtubo sa mga bukog ug kaunoran samtang bata pa.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the material composition of hair and nails (keratin) and mentions animal horns, hooves, and feathers, but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their roles in movement or gathering food as required by G3-L-4.

copy.en:
What are hair and nails made of?

Hair and nails are made of the same tough protein called keratin — the very same stuff found in animal horns, horse hooves, and bird feathers!
copy.tl:
Ano ang gawa ng buhok at kuko?

Ang buhok at kuko ay gawa sa parehong matibay na protina na tinatawag na keratin — ito rin ang bumubuo sa sungay ng hayop, kuko ng kabayo, at balahibo ng ibon!
copy.bis:
Unsay hinimo sa buhok ug kuko?

Ang buhok ug kuko hinimo sa samang lig-on nga protina nga gitawag og keratin — mao gihapon kini ang sangkap sa sungay sa hayop, kuko sa kabayo, ug balhibo sa langgam!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: germs can land on your hands
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions germs (microorganisms) but does not classify living things into groups or use a table. It is about hand hygiene, not classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: germs can land on your hands
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions germs but does not address unicellular vs multicellular organisms. It is about preventing germ spread, not cell structure.

copy.en: Helping change a baby's diaper means germs can land on your hands. Always wash with soap right after, so those germs don't spread to food or other people.
copy.tl: Kapag tumulong kang magpalit ng lampin ng sanggol, may germ na maaaring dumikit sa iyong kamay. Maghugas agad ng sabon para hindi kumalat ang mga ito sa pagkain o sa ibang tao.
copy.bis: Kon motabang ka pag-ilis sa lampin sa bata, mahimong adunay germ sa imong kamot. Panghugas dayon og sabon aron dili mokatap kini ngadto sa pagkaon o sa ubang tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it stops your germs from spreading to people and things around you
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a hygiene tip about handwashing to prevent germ spread. It does not explain how interactions between living things (or living/non-living) bring good or harm, which is the core of G6-L-8. The mention of germs spreading is only tangentially related to interactions causing harm; the card does not teach the concept.

copy.en:
Should you wash your hands even if you're already sick?

Yes! Washing hands after coughing or sneezing won't cure you faster, but it stops your germs from spreading to people and things around you.
copy.tl:
Kailangan pa bang maghugas ng kamay kahit may sakit ka na?

Oo! Ang paghuhugas ng kamay pagkatapos umubo o bumahin ay hindi pampagaling agad, pero pinipigilan nitong kumalat ang germ mo sa iba at sa mga bagay sa paligid.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan pa ba maghugas og kamot bisan sakiton naka?

Oo! Ang paghugas og kamot human mag-ubo o magbahin dili makapaayo dayon, apan makapugong kini nga mokaylap ang imong germ ngadto sa uban ug sa mga butang sa palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Washing your hands often helps keep you from getting diarrhea and other stomach sicknesses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about handwashing preventing diarrhea, a hygiene practice. It does not describe how the digestive system or any other body system works, which is the core of G4-L-1. The mention of stomach sicknesses is only tangentially related to the digestive system.

copy.en: Washing your hands often helps keep you from getting diarrhea and other stomach sicknesses.
copy.tl: Ang madalas na paghuhugas ng kamay ay nakakaiwas sa pagtatae at iba pang sakit sa tiyan.
copy.bis: Ang kanunay nga paghugas sa kamot makapugong sa kalibang ug uban pang sakit sa tiyan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diamond is the hardest natural mineral, rated 10 on the Mohs scale!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about diamond's hardness and Mohs scale rating. It does not involve exploring school grounds, collecting rocks, or describing similarities/differences in features such as texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by the competency. The content is only tangentially related to rocks and minerals.

copy.en:
What is the hardest natural mineral on Earth?

Diamond is the hardest natural mineral, rated 10 on the Mohs scale!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamatigas na likas na mineral sa mundo?

Ang diyamante ang pinakamatigas na likas na mineral, na nasa 10 sa Mohs scale!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakagahi nga natural nga mineral sa kalibutan?

Ang diyamante mao ang pinakagahi nga natural nga mineral, nga 10 sa Mohs scale!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal egg but does not use flow charts, compare life-cycle stages, or address the butterfly/frog/chicken/human examples. It only states a fact about lice eggs, which is not direct support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lice eggs are called nits, and they stick tightly to strands of hair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies lice lay eggs, but it does not identify which groups of animals give birth to live young versus lay eggs, nor does it classify lice among egg-laying groups. The content is only tangentially related to reproduction by eggs.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an egg, which is related to reproduction, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) or explain how lice reproduce. It only names the egg and its attachment, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Lice eggs are called nits, and they stick tightly to strands of hair.
copy.tl: Ang itlog ng kuto ay tinatawag na lisa, at mahigpit itong nakadikit sa hibla ng buhok.
copy.bis: Ang itlog sa kuto gitawag og lisa, ug hugot kini nga nakapilit sa lugas sa buhok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Choosing fruit instead of chips for a snack is healthier
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses nutritional value of snacks (vitamins, fiber, salt, fat), not the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It does not directly support identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Choosing fruit instead of chips for a snack is healthier because fruit has vitamins and fiber, while chips are high in salt and fat.
copy.tl: Mas mainam pumili ng prutas kaysa chips bilang meryenda dahil ang prutas ay may bitamina at hibla, samantalang maraming asin at taba ang chips.
copy.bis: Mas maayo mopili og prutas kaysa chips isip meryenda kay ang prutas adunay bitamina ug fiber, samtang daghan og asin ug tambok ang chips.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When heat energy is added to an object, its temperature rises!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that adding heat raises temperature, but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature (e.g., heat as energy transfer vs. temperature as a measure of average kinetic energy). It only touches on a related relationship.

copy.en:
What happens when we add heat to an object?

When heat energy is added to an object, its temperature rises!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagdagdag tayo ng init sa isang bagay?

Kapag may nadagdag na heat energy sa isang bagay, tumataas ang temperature nito!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung magdugang tag init sa usa ka butang?

Kung adunay madugang nga heat energy sa usa ka butang, mosaka ang temperature niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heat stroke happens when the body can't cool itself anymore
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific failure of body temperature regulation (heat stroke) and its signs, but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it address the indicators named in the competency (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It is only tangentially related to the concept of homeostasis.

copy.en: In the Philippines' hot weather, heat stroke happens when the body can't cool itself anymore — watch for dizziness, hot dry skin, and confusion, and get first aid in the shade right away.
copy.tl: Sa mainit na panahon ng Pilipinas, nangyayari ang heat stroke kapag hindi na kayang palamigin ng katawan ang sarili nito — mga palatandaan ay pagkahilo, mainit at tuyong balat, at pagkalito, kaya kailangan agad ng first aid sa lilim.
copy.bis: Sa init nga panahon sa Pilipinas, mahitabo ang heat stroke kung dili na makapabugnaw ang lawas sa iyang kaugalingon — mga timaan sama sa pagkalipong, init ug uga nga panit, ug pagkalibog, busa kinahanglan dayon og first aid sa landong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If the body gets too hot and can't cool down, heatstroke can happen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions body temperature and heatstroke, which relate to the body temperature indicator of homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it address the other indicators (glucose, blood pressure) or the concept of maintaining balance for survival. It is a safety tip about overheating, not instruction on homeostasis.

copy.en: If the body gets too hot and can't cool down, heatstroke can happen — that's why drinking water and staying in the shade really matters.
copy.tl: Kapag sobrang init at hindi nakakapagpalamig ang katawan, maaaring magka-heatstroke kaya mahalaga ang pag-inom ng tubig at pagpunta sa lilim.
copy.bis: Kon sobra ka init ug dili makapabugnaw ang lawas, mahimong heatstroke, mao nga importante ang pag-inom og tubig ug pagpuyo sa landong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Uranium (atomic number 92) is the heaviest natural element
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses uranium and other heavy elements, but the competency requires identifying names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements. Uranium (Z=92) is neither among the first 20 nor a common element in the intended sense, and the card does not teach element names/symbols as required.

copy.en: Uranium (atomic number 92) is the heaviest natural element found in large amounts, though tiny traces of neptunium and plutonium exist in nature.
copy.tl: Ang uranium (atomic number 92) ang pinakamabigat na natural na elemento nang marami, kahit may napakaliit na trace ng neptunium at plutonium sa kalikasan.
copy.bis: Ang uranium (atomic number 92) mao ang pinakabug-at nga natural nga elemento sa daghang kantidad, bisan adunay gamay kaayo nga trace sa neptunium ug plutonium sa kinaiyahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hedgehogs don't naturally live in the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about hedgehog distribution and does not provide a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat, which is the required format and action of G4-L-4. It only touches on animals and habitats tangentially.

copy.en: Hedgehogs don't naturally live in the Philippines — their true home is Europe, Africa, and parts of Asia.
copy.tl: Ang hedgehog ay hindi katutubo sa Pilipinas; likas itong matatagpuan sa Europa, Africa, at ibang bahagi ng Asya.
copy.bis: Ang hedgehog dili lumad sa Pilipinas; natural kining makit-an sa Europa, Africa, ug uban pang bahin sa Asia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Helium was first discovered in the light of the Sun in 1868
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a scientific discovery (helium found in the Sun) but does not name any scientist or invention, which is the core of the competency. It shares the broad theme of science history but provides no direct instructional support for identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en: Helium was first discovered in the light of the Sun in 1868, before it was found on Earth!
copy.tl: Unang natuklasan ang helium sa liwanag ng araw noong 1868, bago ito nahanap dito sa Earth!
copy.bis: Ang helium una nga nadiskobrehan sa kahayag sa adlaw niadtong 1868, sa wala pa kini makit-i sa Earth!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helium is lighter than air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses helium being lighter than air, which relates to gases but does not teach that matter exists in three states (solids, liquids, gases) or identify states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helium is lighter than air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions helium as a gas implicitly but does not describe properties of gases in terms of shape and volume, nor contrast solids, liquids, and gases.

copy.en:
Why do helium balloons float?

Because helium is lighter than air! That is why balloons filled with it float up high!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang mga lobong puno ng helium?

Dahil ang helium ay mas magaan kaysa hangin! Kaya lumulutang ang mga lobong puno nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong molutaw ang mga balloon nga puno sa helium?

Tungod kay ang helium mas gaan kaysa hangin! Mao nga molutaw ang mga balloon nga puno niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an egret is actually a type of heron
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an egret is actually a type of heron
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Egret versus heron are both birds, not backbone versus no backbone.

copy.en:
Is an egret different from a heron?

Not really — an egret is actually a type of heron! Egrets are usually white, while other herons can be many different colors.
copy.tl:
Iba ba ang egret sa heron?

Hindi pala — ang egret ay isang uri lang ng heron! Karaniwang puti ang egret, samantalang may iba't ibang kulay ang ibang heron.
copy.bis:
Lahi ba ang egret sa heron?

Dili diay — ang egret usa ra ka klase sa heron! Kasagaran puti ang egret, samtang lain-laing kolor ang ubang heron.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold-blooded animals like snakes and lizards slow down a lot in the cold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of temperature affecting animals, but does not describe living things as biotic factors or temperature as an abiotic factor, nor does it use the terms biotic/abiotic. It only illustrates an effect of cold on animals, which is related background but not direct instruction for classifying ecosystem factors.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: slow down a lot in the cold, hiding and barely moving all winter long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

The response is implied but not framed as a characteristic of living things, so it is only related to the competency.

copy.en: Cold-blooded animals like snakes and lizards slow down a lot in the cold, hiding and barely moving all winter long.
copy.tl: Ang mga hayop na malamig ang dugo gaya ng ahas at butiki ay bumabagal nang husto sa lamig, nagtatago at halos hindi gumagalaw sa taglamig.
copy.bis: Ang mga mananap nga bugnaw og dugo sama sa bitin ug tiki mohinay pag-ayo sa bugnaw, motago ug halos dili molihok sa tingtugnaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Before hibernating, animals eat a lot to store body fat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific hibernation behavior (eating to store fat) but does not teach the general concept of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) for all living things. It assumes food is a need rather than identifying it as one.

copy.en:
Why do animals eat so much before hibernating?

Before hibernating, animals eat a lot to store body fat — fuel that keeps them going while they sleep all winter.
copy.tl:
Bakit kumakain nang sobra bago maghibernate ang mga hayop?

Bago maghibernate, kumakain nang marami ang mga hayop para mag-imbak ng taba — ito ang magiging panggatong ng katawan habang natutulog sila.
copy.bis:
Ngano mokaon og daghan ang mananap una maghibernate?

Sa dili pa maghibernate, mokaon og daghan ang mga mananap aron magtigom og tambok — mao kini ang sugnod sa lawas samtang natulog sila.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hiccups, which involve the respiratory/diaphragm, but it does not describe how any human body system works. assignedReviews.card_evidence: hiccups usually go away on their own anyway
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify or describe the nose, windpipe, or lungs, nor explain how the respiratory system works. It only mentions hiccups, a phenomenon loosely connected to breathing, without any direct support for the competency.

copy.en: People try all sorts of tricks to stop hiccups, like drinking water — but honestly, hiccups usually go away on their own anyway!
copy.tl: Marami ang sinusubukan para patigilin ang sinok, gaya ng pag-inom ng tubig — pero kadalasan, nawawala rin naman ito kahit walang ginagawa!
copy.bis: Daghan ang gisulayan aron pahunongon ang sed-ok, sama sa pag-inom og tubig — apan kasagaran, mawala ra kini bisag walay buhaton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The hip bone has a name — it's called the pelvis!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the hip bone as the pelvis. It does not describe how the skeletal system or any body system works, which is the action required by G4-L-1.

copy.en:
What is the hip bone called?

The hip bone has a name — it's called the pelvis!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa buto ng balakang?

May pangalan ang buto ng balakang — tinatawag itong pelvis!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa bukog sa bat-ang?

Adunay ngalan ang bukog sa bat-ang — gitawag kini og pelvis!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A small muscle at the exit of your bladder stays shut tight to hold your pee in
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bladder sphincter muscle holding urine, which touches excretion but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and does not explain how body systems work together.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a muscle and bladder, but it does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. Urinary bladder control is outside the listed systems for this competency.

copy.en: A small muscle at the exit of your bladder stays shut tight to hold your pee in — until you're ready to go to the bathroom.
copy.tl: May maliit na kalamnan sa labasan ng pantog na nakasara nang mahigpit para hindi tumagas ang ihi — hanggang sa handa ka na.
copy.bis: Adunay gamay nga kaunoran sa gawasan sa pantog nga hugot nga sirado aron dili motulo ang ihi — hangtod andam ka na.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about when Homo sapiens appeared. copy.en: Modern humans, also called Homo sapiens, first appeared on Earth about 300,000 years ago!
copy.tl: Ang mga modernong tao o Homo sapiens ay unang lumitaw sa Earth mga 300,000 taon na ang nakalipas!
copy.bis: Ang modernong mga tawo o Homo sapiens unang nitungha sa Yuta mga 300,000 ka tuig na ang milabay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Honey has so little water, plus natural hydrogen peroxide, that bacteria can't grow in it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses why honey does not spoil (food preservation) but does not explain any factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction. The competency specifically requires explaining factors affecting rates of chemical reactions as applied to food preservation; this card provides no such explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Honey has so little water, plus natural hydrogen peroxide, that bacteria can't grow in it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of honey (antibacterial, non-spoiling) but does not describe a chemical property such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. The antibacterial effect is a biological/chemical interaction, not a material's chemical property in the sense of the competency. No direct instructional support for the listed chemical properties.

copy.en:
Why doesn't honey ever spoil?

Honey has so little water, plus natural hydrogen peroxide, that bacteria can't grow in it — it never spoils and can even help small wounds heal!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi nabubulok ang pulot?

Kaunti lang ang tubig sa pulot at may hydrogen peroxide ito, kaya hindi tumutubo ang bacteria dito — hindi ito nabubulok at nakakatulong pa sa maliliit na sugat!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili mabusik ang dugos?

Gamay ra kaayo ang tubig sa dugos ug adunay hydrogen peroxide, mao nga dili motubo ang bacteria niini — dili kini mabusik ug makatabang pa sa gagmay nga samad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they stack in layers by density
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes liquids forming layers by density, which is an example of a non-uniform mixture, but it does not explicitly describe the mixture as uniform/non-uniform, nor does it connect to solutions or suspensions. The focus is on density layering, not on classifying mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pour honey, water, and oil together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves liquids (matter) but does not describe matter as having mass and taking up space. It only shows layering by density, which is a property of matter but not the competency's core concept.

copy.en: Pour honey, water, and oil together, and they stack in layers by density! Honey sits at the bottom, water in the middle, and oil on top.
copy.tl: Paghaluin ang pulot, tubig, at langis, magkakaroon sila ng patong-patong ayon sa densidad! Pulot sa ilalim, tubig sa gitna, at langis sa itaas.
copy.bis: Isagol ang dugos, tubig, ug lana, magpatong-patong sila sumala sa densidad! Dugos sa ubos, tubig sa tunga, ug lana sa ibabaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Drones—the male honeybees—have no stinger
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a body part (stinger) of an animal, but the competency focuses on outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and food gathering. The stinger's absence is not related to movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Drones—the male honeybees—have no stinger at all, so they can never sting you.
copy.tl: Ang mga drone, ang lalaking bubuyog, ay walang tibo kaya hindi sila kailanman makakatusok.
copy.bis: Ang mga drone, ang laking putyokan, walay tusok mao nga dili gyud sila makapaak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A honeybee hive has three kinds of bees: one queen, many workers, and some drones.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the three castes of honeybees but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). It is only related to the topic of insects, not to the classification skill required by the competency.

copy.en: A honeybee hive has three kinds of bees: one queen, many workers, and some drones.
copy.tl: Sa loob ng pukyutan ay may tatlong uri ng bubuyog: isang reyna, maraming manggagawa, at ilang drone.
copy.bis: Ang balay sa putyokan adunay tulo ka klase: usa ka reyna, daghang trabahante, ug pipila ka drone.

A black fungus called sooty mold grows on the sweet, sticky honeydew that drips onto leaves.

Tumutubo ang itim na amag na tinatawag na sooty mold sa matamis na honeydew na natatapon sa dahon.

Nganong naay itom nga agup-op sa dahon?

Motubo ang itom nga agup-op nga gitawag og sooty mold sa matam-is nga honeydew nga matagaktak sa dahon.

copy.tl: Ang hornet ay parang karaniwang putakti pero mas malaki, at kadalasang may malaki at maputlang ulo na madaling makilala.
copy.bis: Ang hornet murag ordinaryong putakti apan mas dako, ug sagad adunay dako ug luspad nga ulo nga sayon mailhan.

copy.tl: Ang bagong-silang na bisiro ay mabilis kumilos — nakakatayo na at nakakalakad ilang oras lang matapos itong isilang.
copy.bis: Ang bag-ong natawo nga nati paspas molihok — makatindog na ug makalakaw pipila lang ka oras human matawo.

Can a horse sleep standing up?

Yes! Its legs can lock in place and won't buckle, so it can sleep while standing.

Kaya bang matulog ang kabayo nang nakatayo?

Oo! Nagki-lock ang mga binti nito at hindi nababaluktot, kaya kaya nitong matulog nang nakatayo.
copy.bis:
Makatulog ba ang kabayo nga nagtindog?

Oo! Ang iyang mga paa makahimo pag-lock ug dili matumba, busa makatulog kini nga nagtindog.

How does a horseshoe crab breathe?

With book gills — thin stacked flaps like pages of a book that pull oxygen from the water.

Paano humihinga ang horseshoe crab?

Gamit ang book gills — manipis na magkakapatong na bahagi na parang pahina ng libro na kumukuha ng oksiheno mula sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagginhawa sa horseshoe crab?

Gamit ang book gills — nipis nga nagsapaw-sapaw nga bahin nga sama sa panid sa libro nga mokuha og oksiheno gikan sa tubig.

Why does food taste dull after eating something too hot?

If your tongue gets burned by very hot food, your sense of taste weakens for a while — until the taste buds heal.
copy.tl:
Bakit parang wala nang lasa ang pagkain pagkatapos kumagat ng mainit?

Kapag napaso ang dila sa sobrang init na pagkain, panandaliang humihina ang panlasa hanggang gumaling ang taste buds.
copy.bis:
Nganong walay lami ang pagkaon human makapaso sa init?

Kung mapaso ang dila sa init kaayo nga pagkaon, mukunhod ang panlasa sa makadiyot hangtod maayo ang taste buds.

Why do people love visiting hot springs in the Philippines?

Many people visit hot springs like those in Los Baños, Laguna, to soak in the warm water and relax! These hot springs are popular tourist spots in some places.

Bakit gusto ng mga tao ang pagbisita sa mga hot springs sa Pilipinas?

Maraming tao ang pumupunta sa mga hot springs tulad ng nasa Los Baños, Laguna, para magbabad sa mainit na tubig at magpahinga! Sikat na tourist spots ang mga ito sa ilang lugar.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ganahan ang mga tawo nga mobisita sa mga hot springs sa Pilipinas?

Daghan ang mga tawo nga moadto sa mga hot springs sama sa Los Baños, Laguna, aron magbabad sa init nga tubig ug mopahulay! Bantog nga tourist spots kini sa pipila ka dapit.

Are all hot springs safe to jump into?

No! Some hot springs are almost boiling hot, so jumping in can be dangerous! Always check how hot the water is before you bathe, so you don't get scalded.

Ligtas bang tumalon sa lahat ng hot springs?

Hindi! May mga hot springs na halos kumukulo, kaya delikadong tumalon dito! Laging suriin muna kung gaano kainit ang tubig bago maligo, para hindi mapaso.
copy.bis:
Luwas ba ang paglukso sa tanang hot springs?

Dili! Adunay mga hot springs nga halos magbukal, mao nga delikado ang paglukso dinhi! Kanunay susihon una kung unsa ka-init ang tubig ayha maligo, aron dili mapaso.

Gumagawa ang butiki ng tunog na 'tik-tik' para makipag-usap sa ibang butiki — minsan para tawagin ang kapareha, minsan para sabihing 'akin ito.'
copy.bis:
Nganong naghimo og 'tik-tik' ang butiki?

Naghimo ang butiki og tingog nga 'tik-tik' aron makigsulti sa ubang butiki — usahay aron tawgon ang kapikas, usahay aron isulti nga 'akoa kini.'

How does a gecko stick to walls?

Its toes are covered underneath with millions of super-tiny hairs, and these grip smooth surfaces so well the gecko never slides down.

Ang ilalim ng kanyang mga daliri ay may milyun-milyong sobrang liliit na balahibo, at mahigpit itong humahawak sa makinis na ibabaw kaya hindi ito nadudulas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdikit sa butiki sa bungbong?

Ang ilalom sa iyang mga tudlo punay milyon-milyong gagmay kaayong balhibo, ug mokupot kini pag-ayo sa hamis nga nawong mao nga dili modahilos ang butiki.

How long does a housefly live?

Only about 28 days! That's the short lifetime of a common housefly.

Gaano katagal nabubuhay ang langaw?

Mga 28 araw lang! Ganito kaikli ang buhay ng isang karaniwang langaw.

Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang langaw?

Mga 28 ka adlaw ra! Mao kini ka mubo ang kinabuhi sa usa ka naandan nga langaw.

A full-grown adult has 32 teeth in total!

Ilang ngipin ang mayroon ang isang may-edad na tao?

May 32 na ngipin ang isang ganap na may-edad na tao!
copy.bis:
Pila ka ngipon ang naa sa usa ka hingkod nga tawo?

Ang hingkod nga tawo adunay 32 ka ngipon!

May 5 pandama ang tao: paningin, pandinig, pang-amoy, panlasa, at pagdama!

Ang tawo adunay 5 ka pamati: panan-aw, pandungog, pangsimhot, pantilaw, ug paghikap!

Ang tawo adunay 24 ka gusok, gihan-ay sa 12 ka paris.

How many bones does an adult have?

206 bones! That's how many an adult human body has, all working together to hold you up.

Ilang buto ang mayroon ang isang matanda?

206 na buto! Ito ang bilang ng buto ng katawan ng isang nasa hustong gulang na tao.

Pila ka bukog ang naa sa usa ka hamtong?

206 ka bukog! Mao kini ang gidaghanon sa bukog sa lawas sa usa ka hamtong nga tawo.
